seven_q.Q0_posture: Analytical and constructive — the document assumes that structural parallels between epidemiology and theology are meaningful and testable.
seven_q.Q1_identity: An isomorphism record (ISO-027) that maps the SIR epidemiological model onto the propagation of sin in communities, with mathematical formalization and biblical support.
seven_q.Q2_domain: Interdisciplinary — primarily epidemiology and theology, with mathematics providing the formal structure.
seven_q.Q3_claim: Sin spreads through communities according to the same population dynamics as infectious diseases, with R₀ = β/γ determining whether sin becomes epidemic or is contained.
seven_q.Q4_support: Ten independent structural correspondences (R₀, β, γ, herd immunity, super-spreaders, quarantine, contact tracing, asymptomatic carriers, vaccination, epidemic curves) plus biblical evidence and empirical social network studies.
seven_q.Q5_dependencies: Depends on the SIR model from epidemiology, social contagion research (Christakis & Fowler), and biblical passages using contagion language.
seven_q.Q6_consequences: Forces that purely individualistic sanctification models are insufficient when R₀ > 1; requires community-level strategies (discipline, discipleship, grace) to contain moral contagion.
seven_q.Q7_kill: Would be falsified if: (1) sinful behaviors show zero social transmission, (2) church discipline has no effect on behavioral spread, (3) spiritual maturity does not confer community protection, (4) leadership sin has equal impact to peripheral sin, or (5) revival/apostasy patterns do not follow S-curves.

graph_summary.one_sentence: ISO-027 establishes a structural isomorphism between the SIR epidemiological model and the propagation of sin in communities, showing that sin spreads through social contact with a reproduction number R₀ that determines whether it becomes epidemic or is contained by grace.
